keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's Ceylon, 1352-1506, and Portuguese Ceylon, 1507-1686, are one-island rows; this dossier continues the Kotte kingdom of ceylon). 'By 1477, a decade after the death of Parakramabahu VI, regional kingdoms had grown in strength'; a rebellion of 1469 made a kingdom in the hill country. The page gives no extent for Kotte in this period, and the Parakramabahu VIII page, opened for it (2026-10-20), none either: it has the Portuguese of 1505 agreeing 'to protect the coastal region' for a tribute of 80 tons of cinnamon and the king dividing the kingdom among his sons. Colombo, Gampaha and Kalutara districts (about 4,800 km2) are my reading and are drawn only as the core.

ledger.note: 1507: the Kotte kingdom stands on its own beside Portuguese Ceylon. 'The Portuguese arrived in Sri Lanka in 1505' and 'successfully secured a trade agreement with the King of Kotte'; 'the Kotte Kingdom became reliant on Portuguese assistance'; the Parakramabahu VIII page has the Portuguese agreeing 'to protect the coastal region' for 'a tribute of 80 tons of cinnamon'. The kingdom itself dates from 1412 (infobox 'Capital moved from Gampola: 1412', 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Gampola') and lasts to 27 May 1597, but the ceylon dossier (sa-04-a) carries it to 1506 as the Sinhalese kingdoms' later phase; 1507 is the year Cliopatria's Portuguese Ceylon begins and this dossier takes over. [Repair 2026-10-20: the dossier began in 1412 and duplicated ceylon's events of 1412-1506 (the rename to Kotte, Jaffna in 1450 and 1467, Kandy in 1469); those events are left to ceylon and jaffna-kingdom.]
1509: 'Parakramabahu IX moved the capital to Kelaniya in 1509, where it stayed until 1528.'

1521: the division. 'The downfall of the Kotte Kingdom began in 1521' with the Vijayaba Kollaya; 'the three sons of King Vijayabahu VII mutinied and killed their father, dividing the kingdom among themselves.' Sitawaka began at Hanwella, Padukka, Kuruwita and Ratnapura.
1521: the Principality of Raigama is the third part of the division. The page names no place; Kalutara district is my reading.
1528 (bridging): the capital 'stayed' at Kelaniya 'until 1528'. The page does not say where it went; Kotte is implied because Dharmapala 'abandoned' the Kotte capital in 1565. Page silent.

By 1564: 'most of the areas of Kotte Kingdom were annexed to the Kingdom of Sitawaka' (no year on the Kotte page). The Sitawaka page has Sitawaka controlling 'much of the kingdom' by 1564, with garrisons at Wattala, Nagalagama and Mapane, and Dharmapala retreating with the Portuguese.
1565: 'In 1565, the capital of Kotte was abandoned by' Dharmapala because of attacks from Sitawaka; he 'was taken to Colombo under Portuguese protection'.

ledger.note: 1594: 'After Sitawaka fell in 1594, these areas were re-annexed to the Kotte kingdom.' The areas are not named; the region is my reading.
27 May 1597: 'Dharmapala formally ceded the Kotte Kingdom to the Portuguese crown' (infobox disestablishment 27 May 1597); the Kotte era ends.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Ceylon 1352-1506 and Portuguese Ceylon 1507-1686 are one-island rows). Three pages (Kotte opened twice; Sitawaka and Kandy as mirrors). The Kotte page is short on dates and boundaries and contradicts itself: Kotte is established in 1412 and 1415; the Portuguese arrive in 1505 and the page has no 1518 fort; Bhuvanekabahu VII has no dates; the page has no 1543 or 1580 events.
Disagreements: (1) Kandy is 'initially a client kingdom' of Kotte (Kandy page) against 'a rebellion ... in 1469' (this page): no vassal pair written; (2) Jaffna: Cliopatria's Jaffna Kingdom row (1314-1594) and the page's 'unifying the entire island' in 1450; the page dates the reversal nowhere; (3) Cliopatria begins Portuguese Ceylon in 1507, while Kotte lasts to 27 May 1597.
Not settled: the extent in every period (the lowlands round Colombo are my reading); the Raigama place (Kalutara, a guess); the capital after 1528; the Sitawaka annexation year (a 'by 1564'); what the Portuguese held; the 1580 donation of Kotte to the Portuguese king (not on the page).
Counterparts needing a dossier: principality-of-raigama (1521-1538); jaffna-kingdom is a Cliopatria row (sa-04-a); portuguese-ceylon and ceylon are Cliopatria rows.

[Repair 2026-10-20, sa-04-x-fix] One state in one dossier: the dossier began in 1412, but ceylon (sa-04-a) lists 'Kingdom of Kotte' as an alt name and carries the same events (/ledger/12 rename to Kotte 1412, /ledger/14 Jaffna 1450, /ledger/15 Jaffna 1467, /ledger/16 Kandy 1469), and jaffna-kingdom mirrors 1450 and 1467 with ceylon. This dossier now starts in 1507, the year Cliopatria's Portuguese Ceylon begins, as the continuation of ceylon. Removed here (left to ceylon and jaffna-kingdom; recorded so a repair that ends ceylon in 1412 can restore them): found 1412 (Parakramabahu VI, Gampola to Kotte, confidence 2) and the capital of 1415 (the infobox says 1412, one sentence of the text 1415); 1450 gain of the Jaffna kingdom (Yapanaya, Kilinochchi, Mannarama, Mulativ and Vavuniya districts, confidence 3) and of the rest of the island from 'nobody' (confidence 2); 1467 loss of Jaffna to jaffna-kingdom (confidence 1, the page gives no year; jaffna-kingdom has 1467 at confidence 3 on its own page); 1469 loss of the hill country to kingdom-of-kandy (confidence 3) and of the rest of the island to 'nobody' (confidence 1); the keyframes of 1412-1449 (three districts), 1450-1466 (the whole island) and 1467-1468 (the island without Jaffna); the war 'Kotte conquest of Jaffna'; Parakramabahu VI (1412-1467) on the ruler strip. The orchestrator should have ceylon's owner add kingdom-of-kotte among its successors (or end ceylon in 1412 and take 1412-1506 back into this dossier, the choice closer to the Kotte page). Radius: the circle round Avissawella is 25 km here as in kingdom-of-sitawaka (it was 40 km and swallowed Kotte); the 1521-1563 shape was one cell and is now Colombo and Gampaha less that circle (about 1,000 km2, four cells). Extent 1469-1520: the Parakramabahu VIII page was opened and is silent on territory, so the three districts stay a reading. The Portuguese agreement of 1505 (protection of the coast for a tribute of 80 tons of cinnamon, Parakramabahu VIII page) is a protectorate or tributary relation that is not modelled (no end short of the cession of 1597); sa-06's portuguese-ceylon owner may carry it. Capitals: the first capital now starts in 1507 because the dossier does; Kotte has been the capital since 1412 (infobox).
